item: Recovery hardening — undecryptable MFA secrets, restore ordering
scope: code only; no lab, no stack started, no image built, no restore run
register_rows_changed: none — REC-02 was already PASS; these were 'recorded, not fixed' findings

repos.vidra-user: untouched — the playlist-delete confirmation is recorded for a later UI slice

before.observed: A37 negative control (a), and reproduced here as a unit RED before any change

after.parity: byte-identical to the wrong-code 401 apart from request_id, asserted by decoding both bodies and deleting that key
after.why_indistinguishable: a distinguishable answer would let an unauthenticated caller enumerate which accounts an instance can no longer verify

a37_1_undecryptable_mfa_secret.audit: ActionMFAChallenge / failure / reason=secret_undecryptable; the enrollment-verify half uses ActionMFAEnable with the same reason and its own wrong-code 400
a37_1_undecryptable_mfa_secret.mechanism: openTOTPSecret returned a bare error, which reaches echo's handler unclassified so the only status left is 500; it now returns *auth.MFASecretUndecryptableError, unwrapping to auth.ErrMFASecretUndecryptable

recovery_codes.storage: SHA-256 hex of the canonicalised code (issueRecoveryCodes -> hashRecoveryCode)
recovery_codes.path: CompleteMFAChallenge routes anything that is not six digits to UseRecoveryCode, which never touches the cipher
recovery_codes.proven: a recovery code completes the challenge with 200 and a full session on the SAME row whose TOTP secret is undecryptable

a37_2_kek_mismatch_surfaced.before: the KEK is validated for SHAPE at boot and never against a stored ciphertext, so a wrong-KEK restore boots, answers /readyz 200 and serves everything except a second-factor login

check.query: ListRecentUserMFASecrets — SELECT user_id, totp_secret_sealed FROM user_mfa ORDER BY created_at DESC, user_id LIMIT $1
check.why_a_sample: the question is whether this KEK belongs to this database, which one row answers as well as ten thousand; it sits on the boot path
check.timeout: 5s bounded context; a read failure is logged and the component reports not_configured

component.name: mfa_kek

states.ok: every sampled sealed secret opens, or nobody has ever enrolled
states.degraded: at least one sampled sealed secret cannot be opened; the message names the count and MFA_KEY_KEK
states.not_configured: the check did not run (unit servers, embedders, a read failure)

component.readiness_effect: none — /readyz still answers 200; the top-level body status now reads degraded rather than ok when any component is degraded
component.why_not_down: an operator who has just restored with the wrong KEK must be able to log in with a password to fix it; 503ing the api is the one thing that would stop them

a37_2_kek_mismatch_surfaced.vidra_doctor: no KEK check exists to extend — nothing in internal/doctor opens a stored ciphertext, so nothing was added
a37_2_kek_mismatch_surfaced.openapi: ComponentStatus.status description corrected to ok | degraded | down | not_configured (it said ok, down, not_configured)

a37_3_restore_ordering.before: stop api/search/frontend was the first thing after the confirmation prompt, so a corrupt archive or a refused schema pairing took the site down and THEN correctly refused to change anything
after_order: docker cp the archive into the postgres container
a37_3_restore_ordering.invariant: every step above the stop only reads, so every refusal now happens with the stack still serving
a37_3_restore_ordering.docs: deploy/README.md's restore paragraph rewritten to match

a37_4_gzip_guard.before_output: [restore] decompressing vidra-corrupt.dump.gz / gzip: invalid compressed data--crc error / gzip: <path>: uncompress failed
a37_4_gzip_guard.before_missing: no [restore] ERROR: line — set -e had the exit code right and said nothing
a37_4_gzip_guard.after: || die on the *.gz) branch AND on the plain cp branch beside it, both messages stating that nothing was stopped and nothing was dropped

a11_media_gc.finding_confirmed: a media-GC sweep writes no job_runs row, and it cannot
a11_media_gc.mechanism: job_runs is a projection maintained by AFTER triggers on the durable QUEUE tables (0083, extended by 0094, 0107, 0120); a scheduled sweep has no queue row to project
a11_media_gc.wider_finding: NO scheduled pass in vidra-core records a job run — not runMediaGCWorker, not runTelemetryRetentionWorker, not the media-hash backfill; jobloop.Loop has no repository at all
a11_media_gc.not_done: giving scheduled work a queue table is a design change, not a hardening slice

done_instead.why_one_helper: an admin's sweep and the scheduled one must be filterable the same way
done_instead.vocabulary: breaker_tripped added to internal/audit allowedMetadataKeys — that allowlist refuses the WHOLE event on an unknown key, so the acceptance is pinned by its own test in internal/audit

recorded_not_fixed: Neither delete control in vidra-user's PlaylistDetailView has a confirmation step, while the Studio video delete is two-step and the GC purge demands a typed PURGE. This slice is code-only in core and meta and deliberately did not touch vidra-user.

vidra-core.make ci: exit 0 — fmt-check, vet, migrate-lint, openapi-verify, sqlc-verify, test-race

meta.bash -n: clean on every deploy/*.sh, bootstrap.sh, install.sh, tests/*.sh
meta.profile render: postgres, redis, search, migrate, search-migrate and prep-volumes publish NO ports; api 127.0.0.1:8080, frontend 127.0.0.1:3000

red_first.core: TestMFAChallengeWithAnUndecryptableSecretIsIndistinguishableFromAWrongCode failed with 'undecryptable-secret status = 500, want 401' before the fix
red_first.meta: the three new restore tests were run against origin/main's restore.sh and all three failed: "'[restore] ERROR:' not found in '[restore] decompressing vidra-corrupt.dump.gz\ngzip: invalid compressed data--crc error…'" and '6382 not less than 6081 : the archive must be decompressed before the site is stopped'
red_first.meta_rollback: the four new rollback.sh tests were run against origin/main's script: three assertions failed and one errored, because restore_env_and_die did not exist to extract
red_first.core_doctor: TestSchemaLedgerAheadOfTheBinary failed against origin/main's checks_state.go with 'status = ok, want warn (detail: the core migration ledger (schema_migrations) is at version 136 and clean)'

not_lab_observed: the 500 was reproduced as a unit RED, not against a live wrong-KEK instance
the boot WARN and the mfa_kek component are exercised through fake repositories, not a real user_mfa table
the new restore.sh ordering is asserted over the script's own text and its extracted decompression block, not by watching a real archive fail on a real host
no stack was started, no image was built, no restore was run
restore_env_and_die is driven as an extracted shell function over a temporary env file, not by a rollback that really failed to pull
doctor's ledger-ahead warning comes from a fake host scripted to answer 136 and 135, not from a rolled-back stack

a38r_1_doctor_ledger_ahead.before: on the rolled-back stack (v0.6.3-a37 binaries, ledger 136) vidra doctor printed a green '✓ schema ledger: the core migration ledger (schema_migrations) is at version 136 and clean' — true about the ledger, silent about the one fact that distinguishes it from a matched deployment
a38r_1_doctor_ledger_ahead.red: status = ok, want warn (detail: the core migration ledger (schema_migrations) is at version 136 and clean)
a38r_1_doctor_ledger_ahead.after_detail: schema ledger 136 is ahead of this binary's newest migration 135 — this release can run on it, but a newer release was deployed; roll forward or expect no new migrations to apply
a38r_1_doctor_ledger_ahead.why_warn: the state is SUPPORTED — one release of backward compatibility is the release policy, the migrator no-ops rather than failing, and an operator who has just completed a successful app-only rollback is looking at exactly this; a ✗ would tell them to undo what they meant to do

embedded_max_source.bundled_postgres: docker compose exec -T api /app/api migrate embedded-max — the RUNNING IMAGE, over the same exec that read 'migrate version', because the container is what serves and the operator's vidra binary may be built from a different checkout than VIDRA_CORE_TAG
embedded_max_source.managed_database: dbmigrate.EmbeddedMax() in process — the same embedded-FS walk the migrator itself reads

a38r_1_doctor_ledger_ahead.fix_text_quotes: dbmigrate.LedgerAheadMessage, so an operator grepping the deploy output and an operator reading doctor see the same sentence

states_pinned_by_test.ledger behind the binary: ok (the ordinary 'there are migrations to apply' state)
states_pinned_by_test.dirty AND ahead: still the dirty FAIL — a half-applied migration is the more urgent fact and has the runbook behind it
states_pinned_by_test.image cannot answer embedded-max: silent (ok) — 'I could not check' must never render as 'checked and fine'

a38r_1_doctor_ledger_ahead.search_ledger: deliberately NOT compared: vidra-search's migrations are compiled into ITS binary and the only number available from here is core's, which would be a confident lie rather than a silence

a38r_2_rollback_env_restore.before: every refusal between the set_key rewrite and `up -d` leaves the RUNNING STACK untouched, but two of them left env/production.env pinned to the ROLLBACK TARGET; the pull message read '($ENV_FILE restored from ${ENV_FILE}.bak if you need to undo)', which mid-incident reads as a statement that it HAD been restored

uneven_before.pull: did not, and said something that reads as if it had

a38r_2_rollback_env_restore.after: one restore_env_and_die helper on all five paths (three checkout failures, config -q, pull); a test counts its uses over the CODE so a sixth path cannot be added without it
a38r_2_rollback_env_restore.missing_bak: the helper says 'could not restore' and names backups/env-history/ instead of claiming a restore — the one thing worse than not restoring is saying you did
a38r_2_rollback_env_restore.partial_checkout_sweep: a repo that already moved is NOT moved back, and the message says so: the next deploy or rollback re-syncs every checkout from the env file, and unwinding a partial sweep would be a second thing that can fail mid-incident

a38r_3: closed by the A37-3 change above — it re-logged A37-3 against the two new restore.sh refusals (dirty dump, pinned image below the dump's schema), and all three now happen with the site still serving
